tools.name: book
tools.description: your book again (positions, cash, P&L), the session and the limits code enforces right now. Args: {}.

tools.name: option_menu
tools.description: the liquid option contracts you may buy on a stock: calls and puts in the allowed expirations, with bid, ask, delta, IV and open interest. A buy_option must copy its contracts from this list. Args: {symbol}.

symbol.description: A US ticker in uppercase, e.g. NVDA.

tools.name: quote
tools.description: the live price of a stock, its bid and ask when the broker streams it, and the day's change. Args: {symbol}.

symbol.description: A US ticker in uppercase, e.g. NVDA.

tools.name: technicals
tools.description: a stock's technicals from Alpaca's bars: daily (20/50/200-day averages, 52-week high, 5/20-day returns, ATR, RSI, 20-day range) and today's 5-minute (VWAP, opening range, RSI, EMA trend). Args: {symbol}.

symbol.description: A US ticker in uppercase, e.g. NVDA.

tools.name: news
tools.description: what our feeds saw about a stock (or the market, symbol null) in the last N hours, most severe first, with article summaries. Args: {symbol|null, hours 1-72}.

anyOf.description: A US ticker in uppercase, e.g. NVDA.

tools.name: dossier
tools.description: our feeds' dossier on up to 5 stocks: the top items of the last 72 h, market-wide items, scheduled releases, moves nothing explains and items nobody confirmed. Args: {symbols}.

items.description: A US ticker in uppercase, e.g. NVDA.

tools.name: item
tools.description: one news item in full by the id the news tool shows (its first 12 characters are enough): title, source, confirmations, article summary and key points. Args: {id}.

id.description: The item id, or its first 12 characters.

tools.name: past_decisions
tools.description: the bot's last decisions on a stock and its options (yours, and the bot's earlier ones before you took over), with what came of them. Args: {symbol}.

symbol.description: A US ticker in uppercase, e.g. NVDA.

tools.name: calendar
tools.description: scheduled US macro releases (FOMC, CPI, jobs, PPI, PCE, GDP) in the next N days. Args: {days 1-14}.

tools.name: history
tools.description: a stock's daily history from our history store (years deep): return, range, volatility, worst drawdown, biggest days, weekly closes. Args: {symbol, days 7-1825}.

symbol.description: A US ticker in uppercase, e.g. NVDA.

tools.name: past_news
tools.description: earlier news about a stock from our archive (beyond the last 30 days too), most severe first, with the price move 1 h, 1 d and 5 d after each. Args: {symbol, days 7-730}.

symbol.description: A US ticker in uppercase, e.g. NVDA.
The stock, or the option's UNDERLYING stock for option actions.

action.description: Stocks you don't hold: buy (opens a position; never adds). Stocks you hold (YOUR BOOK): sell some or all, adjust_exits (new stop and target), or hold. Options: buy_option opens one from an option_menu result (symbol = the underlying); close_option or hold_option manage an open options position by its structure_id.

allocation_pct.description: Stock buy only: % of total account equity to commit (e.g. 8 means 8%). null otherwise.

sell_pct.description: Stock sell only: % of the currently held shares to sell, 1-100 (100 = close the position). null otherwise.

stop_loss.description: Stocks (buy, adjust_exits): stop-loss trigger in dollars, BELOW the current price. Options: the UNDERLYING price that proves the trade wrong (below the current price for calls and call spreads, above it for puts and put spreads); the position is closed when the stock crosses it. null = none.

take_profit.description: Stocks (buy, adjust_exits): take-profit limit in dollars, ABOVE the current price. Options: the UNDERLYING price at which to take profit (above for calls, below for puts). null = none.

horizon.description: intraday = flat by the close. overnight = may carry to tomorrow. multi_day = swing position (every options position is multi_day).

conviction.description: 1-10. Below the minimum in CONTEXT means do not open a trade.

rationale.description: 1-3 sentences: why this, why now. Cite numbers from the brief or your tool results.

evidence.description: 2-5 concrete facts with numbers or times, from the brief or your tool results.

invalidation.description: The specific price/event that proves the idea wrong.

structure_id.description: close_option / hold_option: the id of an options position in YOUR BOOK. null otherwise.

strategy.description: long_call / long_put = buy one contract type. call_debit_spread = buy a call and sell a higher-strike call, same expiration. put_debit_spread = buy a put and sell a lower-strike put, same expiration.

long_leg.description: The contract to BUY, copied exactly from an option_menu result in this episode, e.g. NVDA261120C00140000.

short_leg.description: Spreads only: the contract to SELL, copied exactly from the same option_menu result, same expiration as long_leg. null for long_call / long_put.

premium_pct.description: % of account equity to spend on premium (at most the per-position cap in YOUR BOOK's options limits).

stop_loss_pct.description: Exit when the position is worth this % less than was paid, e.g. 50. null = the default.

take_profit_pct.description: Take profit when the position is worth this % more than was paid, e.g. 100. null = the default.

option.description: buy_option only: what to buy, from an option_menu result in this episode. null for every other action.

decisions.description: Only about what woke you and what you hold: at most 3 new entries (buy, buy_option), plus one for each position in YOUR BOOK that needs a decision. An empty list is a normal answer: watch instead of acting early.

kind.description: price_above / price_below: wake when the symbol trades above / below `level`. move_pct: wake when it moves `level` % either way from now. news: wake when an item about the symbol (null = market-wide) reaches severity `level` (0-100). time: wake at `at`.

symbol.description: The symbol exactly as listed. null only for news and time watches about the whole market.

level.description: The price, the % move or the minimum severity, as `kind` says. null for time watches.

at.description: time watches only: when to wake, as an ISO date-time with its offset. null otherwise.

hours.description: How long the watch lasts, 1-168 hours.

priority.description: risk = something you hold is in danger; opportunity = a possible entry; review = anything else.

note.description: At most 300 characters: what to check when it fires. You will see it then.

watches.description: 0-5 conditions to wake you on. Prefer a watch to deciding early.

cancel_watches.description: Ids of your own watches (from YOUR WATCHES) that no longer matter.

subject.description: A symbol exactly as listed, MARKET or BOOK.

text.description: At most 500 characters you want to see in your next brief on this subject (kept 14 days).

notes.description: 0-3 notes for later: a level that matters, what you are waiting for, what you learned.

reply.description: 1-3 sentences in plain English: what you saw and what you did about it. To an owner's question: the answer.
